subject: general
question: A dealer marks his goods at 80% above the cost price and allows a discount of 5% on the marked price. What is his gain or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit % = x + y + (xy / 100)

Here, Markup (x) = +80 and Discount (y) = −5

Net Profit % = 80 − 5 + [80 × (−5) / 100]

Net Profit % = 75 − 400/100 = 75 − 4 = 71%

**∴ Answer = 71% gain**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup % = 80%, Discount % = 5%

**Formula used:**

MP = CP × (100 + Markup %)/100; SP = MP × (100 − Discount %)/100; Profit % = (SP − CP)/CP × 100

 
• 
• 
• CP = 100 MP = 180 SP = 171 
 Markup +80% 
 −5% Discount Net Profit = 71% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100 units

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 80% of 100 = 180 units

⇒ Discount = 5% of 180 = (5 × 180) / 100 = 9 units

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 180 − 9 = 171 units

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 171 − 100 = 71 units

⇒ Profit % = (71 / 100) × 100 = 71%

**∴ The correct answer is (2).**
